utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We have now a Status Conference in the case of Prosecutor versus Milan Martic. May I ask the registry to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning everybody in the courtroom. This is case number IT-95-11-A, the Prosecutor versus Milan Martic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Martic, may I ask you, can you follow the proceedings in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I have the appearances, please. The moving party in principle is the Defence, therefore the appearances for Mr. Martic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. On behalf of the Defence, on behalf of Mr. Martic, I appear here as his Defence lawyer, my name is Predrag Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Paul Rogers on behalf of the Prosecutor; assisted by co-counsel, Nicole Lewis; and our case manager this morning, Lourdes Galicia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The agenda should be to hear first issues related to the health condition and detention conditions, and then primarily the question of the deadlines. Of course then finally there will be some room to address issues parties want to raise. Let me start with asking Mr. Martic himself, do you have any extraordinary health problems or any problems as regards the detention conditions in the United Nations Detention Unit? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Concerning this question of the protocol nature, I will tell you the following. Despite of the trial inquisition, I am, thank God, fine. I do not wish to speak about the conditions in the Detention Unit, it's quite well-known. If you are interested, you will be able to see for yourself that this was indeed a case of a trial inquisition; if you have no interest in that, then God help you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Normally I wouldn't respond to such a remark, but please be assured that all the five Judges on the bench as professional Judges will proceed impartial and conscientiously as possible, and in particular as we are working under partly driven common-law system, we will listen carefully what the parties, and in particular you, the appellant, will have to say. Coming into this courtroom, we enter into the courtroom with a white sheet of paper, and of course the appeal is not a trial de novo, but we will go in all the details, whether there are merits of your appeal or not. Pleased take this as granted. I think one of the most important issues, as usual, in the beginning of an appeal is the question of time-limits. The Chamber issued two decisions, one of 21 September 2007, ordering the appellant to file the appellant's brief no later than 24 December 2007, and directing the registrar to provide B/C/S translation of the judgement to the appellant and his counsel by 7 December 2007 at the latest, with a view to my clock I can see this time has already expired, so we have to find new deadlines. As regards the question of response by -- we stated in our decision of -- I think it was 31 October that the deadline would be seven days after the rendering of the -- or the filing of the judgement in B/C/S. The problem is that some research shows clearly that our translation unit will not be able to present a correct and conscientious translation of the judgement into B/C/S by 24 December 2007. We have always to see this, that it's not safe-guarded, maybe it will be a little bit delayed; and we have to take into account additionally that the court management system has advised that after receiving the translation from CLSS they will still need some days to get the judgement ready for filing. Having said this, I think it would be advisable and also with a view to the holidays we will have in the beginning of the year in the area of former Yugoslavia that we aim at having both response and the appeal brief ready by Monday, 14 January. However, in case the filing is not completed by January 2, I would suggest that then the deadline runs as of the day of the filing in B/C/S and then the allotted time, seven days for the response and 14 days for the appeals brief would run as of the day of the filing. May I hear the parties on this, whether they have objections or not. Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of the Prosecution, no, we don't have any objection to that course of action. I was -- if we were on the original timetable, I was going to address Your Honour on that original timetable and request an extension of time in any event because of the impact of the Christmas break and the three days that were lost in the briefing period. But as Your Honour has anticipated and already found out that it's unlikely that that timetable can be held to, I don't need to address you on that and we're content with the timetable that you outline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I hear the Defence on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the existing situation, it is important for the Defence, in compliance with the decision of the 21st of September, 2007, it is important for us to have the 14-day deadline after receiving the translation to consult the accused and to then write the appeals brief. I'm not quite clear on interpreting the deadline, seven days for filing response and 14 days for appeals brief. Having heard the explanation - and you can correct me if I'm wrong - it seems that the Prosecution has to write a response before we file our appeals brief or before the deadline runs out. I don't know if I'm interpreting this correctly. Could you please clarify this for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course I will. We have two different scenarios before us. One there -- we have the appeal lodged by Prosecution, and then it would be to respond and to reply; and on the other hand, we have your appeal and as a matter of fairness, as usual, even though you can already now discuss the merits with Mr. Martic himself, it is indeed necessary that having the text in writing before you, that you are able to discuss other matters together with your client. Thus, I said in the beginning, in principle it doesn't make sense to have two different deadlines. Thus, the deadline for both filings and summations would expire on 14 January. However, only this with the caveat that it's finally cited already today. The deadline -- let me say this also because it doesn't help also the Chamber. The deadline for both decisions will start, if it was not filed before the 1st of January, the very day of the filing of the B/C/S translation by the registry. Is it fair enough for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I, as usual, when having the first Status Conference on appeal, may I invite both parties to rethink whether or not they want to uphold with a view to the final judgement all reasons of appeal. Having been Defence counsel in the past, I know that it can be sometimes dangerous to overload an appeal because then the Judges would look into all details and in all reasons of the appeal in the same way, and not as maybe the parties wishes to focus on a concrete, serious issue where a party might believe that the decision of the first-instance was wrong and this error needs to be corrected. So I think focusing on the main points of appeal is always a value in itself. Having said this, I think in order to avoid unnecessary filings, we should also right now discuss the date of the next Status Conference, which is due within 120 days as of now. And my suggestion would be, as we have this chance only every four years, to have the next Status Conference on Friday, the 29 February, 2008. Would this be agreeable for both parties? First the Defence because, no doubt, the Defence has sometimes more problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It suits us. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any other issues to be raised by the parties. Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That's not the case. Thank you very much, and let's meet on 29 February. A final schedule in particular at which time and in which room will follow in writing. Thank you. The Status Conference stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: adjourned at 9.20 a.m. 24 25
